\section{Higher-degree simple-Parry causal obstructions}
\label{sec:simple-parry-causal-obstructions}

The equalities between bounded-multiple order and optimal causal inverse
length proved in Theorem~\ref{thm:quadratic-optimal-causal-inverse} do not
extend universally beyond the stated quadratic cases.  We now identify the
finite object that governs
causal inversion in arbitrary simple-Parry rank folds and exhibit
higher-degree counterexamples in both directions.  This section continues to
concern the cyclic language rank of this article, not equality of numerical
$\beta$-values.

Recall that Pisot bases have eventually periodic greedy expansions of one
\cite{Schmidt1980}, whereas the finite expansion required below is the
additional simple-Parry hypothesis.  Parry admissibility and the associated
Bertrand numeration are standard
\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}; the expansions of one for
cubic Pisot numbers were classified by Bassino \cite{Bassino2002}.  We record
the data needed
to distinguish these published inputs from the new sliding-congruence
statement.

Let $\beta\notin\mathbb Z$ be a simple-Parry Pisot number with
\[
d_\beta(1)=t_1t_2\cdots t_p0^\infty,
\qquad t_1=d=\lfloor\beta\rfloor,
\qquad t_p>0,
\]
where $p\ge2$ and $0\le t_i\le d$.  Put
\[
P_\beta(z)=z^p-t_1z^{p-1}-\cdots-t_p,
\qquad
\mathcal A_d=\{0,1,\ldots,d\},
\qquad
\Delta_d=[-d,d]\cap\mathbb Z.
\]
The raw system is the full shift $\mathcal A_d^{\mathbb Z}$, so $\Delta_d$
is exactly its digit-difference alphabet.  Let $Q_n$ be the number of legal
length-$n$ words.  In the low-to-high convention used throughout this
article, the established Parry--Bertrand rank data are
\begin{align}
Q_0&=1,\nonumber\\
Q_n&=1+\sum_{i=1}^n t_iQ_{n-i} &&(1\le n<p),\label{eq:simple-parry-Q}\\
Q_n&=\sum_{i=1}^p t_iQ_{n-i} &&(n\ge p),\nonumber
\end{align}
and
\[
\Rank_{\beta,m}(w)=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}w_jQ_j
\]
maps the legal length-$m$ words, in colexicographic order, bijectively onto
$\{0,\ldots,Q_m-1\}$.  We therefore define $\Fold_{\beta,m}$ and
$\Phi_{\beta,m}$ by the same rank reduction modulo $Q_m$ as in
Definition~\ref{def:quadratic-parry-fold}.

For $m\ge2$, define
\begin{equation}
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
=\min\{L\ge1:a_t=\psi(y_t,\ldots,y_{t+L-1})
\text{ for every }y=\Phi_{\beta,m}(a)\},
\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-length}
\end{equation}
with value $\infty$ if no such $L$ exists.  Also set
\[
\mathfrak a(P_\beta,d)
=\min\{\deg H:0\ne H\in(P_\beta),\ H(0)\ne0,
\ |[z^j]H|\le d\text{ for all }j\}.
\]

\begin{proposition}[Degeneration of the bounded-multiple order]
\label{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order}
Under the preceding simple-Parry hypotheses,
\[
\mathfrak a(P_\beta,d)=p.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The coefficient vector of $P_\beta$ consists of the leading coefficient
$1$ and the coefficients $-t_1,\ldots,-t_p$.  It lies in $\Delta_d$, and its
constant coefficient $-t_p$ is nonzero.  Hence
$\mathfrak a(P_\beta,d)\le p$.  Conversely, every nonzero member of the
principal ideal $(P_\beta)\subset\mathbb Z[z]$ has degree at least
$\deg P_\beta=p$.  This proves equality.
\end{proof}

For $L\ge1$, introduce the bounded sliding-congruence obstruction
\begin{equation}
\mathcal N_{\beta,m,L}
=\left\{e\in\Delta_d^{m+L-1}:
e_0\ne0,\quad
\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}Q_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}
\ (0\le t<L)\right\}.
\label{eq:bad-sliding-congruence-set}
\end{equation}
Equivalently, let $T_{m,L}$ be the $L$-row banded Toeplitz matrix obtained by
placing the kernel $(Q_0,\ldots,Q_{m-1})$ at offsets
$t=0,\ldots,L-1$.  Then the last condition is
$T_{m,L}e\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.

\begin{theorem}[Exact causal collision criterion]
\label{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}
For every nonintegral simple-Parry Pisot number as above and every $m\ge2$,
\begin{equation}
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
=\min\{L\ge1:\mathcal N_{\beta,m,L}=\varnothing\},
\label{eq:exact-causal-obstruction}
\end{equation}
where the minimum is $\infty$ when all the obstruction sets are nonempty.

More explicitly, let $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ be the directed graph with vertex set
$V=\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  There is an edge from
$v=(v_0,\ldots,v_{m-2})$ to $w=(w_0,\ldots,w_{m-2})$ precisely when
\[
w_i=v_{i+1}\quad(0\le i<m-2)
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\sum_{j=0}^{m-2}Q_jv_j+Q_{m-1}w_{m-2}
\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}.
\label{eq:collision-graph-edge}
\end{equation}
If $B=\{v\in V:v_0\ne0\}$, then
\begin{equation}
\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
=1+\sup\{\text{number of edges in a directed path starting in }B\}.
\label{eq:collision-graph-longest-path}
\end{equation}
The supremum is infinite exactly when a directed cycle is reachable from
$B$.  Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
\Phi_{\beta,m}\text{ is injective}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Gamma_{\beta,m}\text{ has no bi-infinite path other than the zero path}.
\label{eq:collision-graph-injectivity}
\end{equation}
If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, then its causal inverse is finite exactly
when the zero vertex is not reachable from $B$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let $u,v\in\mathcal A_d^{m+L-1}$ and put $e_i=u_i-v_i$.  Since the legal
rank is a bijection, the $t$th output symbols of the two blocks are equal if
and only if their raw ranks agree modulo $Q_m$, namely if and only if
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}Q_je_{t+j}\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}.
\]
Moreover, $u_0\ne v_0$ if and only if $e_0\ne0$.  Thus every pair of raw
blocks whose first symbols remain ambiguous after $L$ outputs determines an
element of $\mathcal N_{\beta,m,L}$.

Conversely, for any $e\in\Delta_d^{m+L-1}$ define coordinatewise
\[
u_i=\max\{e_i,0\},\qquad v_i=\max\{-e_i,0\}.
\]
Then $u_i,v_i\in\mathcal A_d$, $u_i-v_i=e_i$, and both finite blocks extend
arbitrarily to points of the full shift.  Hence every element of
$\mathcal N_{\beta,m,L}$ is realized by an actual output collision with
distinct first symbols.  If the obstruction set is empty, the first raw
symbol is constant on every fiber over an occurring length-$L$ output word;
the resulting function on this finite output language is the decoder $\psi$
in \eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-length}.  This proves
\eqref{eq:exact-causal-obstruction}.

A length-$L$ path in $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ beginning at
$(e_0,\ldots,e_{m-2})\in B$ is exactly a vector
$e\in\mathcal N_{\beta,m,L}$: each edge appends one coordinate and imposes
one of the $L$ congruences.  Formula
\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} follows.  Since the graph is finite,
arbitrarily long such paths exist exactly when a directed cycle is reachable
from $B$.

A bi-infinite difference sequence labels a bi-infinite path in the graph if
and only if all corresponding output ranks agree.  Every coordinate of that
difference sequence is realized by two raw digits by the positive--negative
part construction above.  Therefore a nonzero bi-infinite graph path is
equivalent to a pair of distinct points with the same image, proving
\eqref{eq:collision-graph-injectivity}.

Finally assume injectivity.  No directed cycle containing a nonzero vertex
can then occur, because its periodic repetition would be a nonzero
bi-infinite path.  The zero loop is consequently the only cycle reachable
from $B$ that is compatible with injectivity.  Thus paths from $B$ have
unbounded length exactly when they reach the zero vertex.  Combining this
with \eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
\end{enumerate}
If these conditions hold, then
\begin{equation}
1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
\end{equation}
If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
bounded periodic certificate.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.

Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.

If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
may be chosen simple.

In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
Set
\[
c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
\]
Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
\[
Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
\]
Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
  \[
  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
  \]
  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
\end{enumerate}
For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.

An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
\end{equation}
The left side has modulus at most
$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
edge set is
\[
\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
\qquad
\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
\]

When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
The only raw realization of either is the pair
$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
classification.
\end{proof}

The graph in Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} is the arithmetic
specialization of the standard fiber-product collision graph for a sliding
block code; see \cite{LindMarcus1995,Nasu1995}.  Its substantive role here is
that it separates the exact modulus-$Q_m$ survival depth from the unrelated
degree of a bounded polynomial multiple.

We next show that, even in algebraic degree three, the causal lengths at
injective apertures have no uniform bound.  Bassino's classification
\cite{Bassino2002} contains the cubic Pisot family and its finite expansion
of one used below.  We include a direct verification of those input data so
that the new part of the argument is visibly confined to the sliding
collision depth.

For $n\ge4$, put
\begin{equation}
M_n(x)=x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n
\label{eq:cubic-unbounded-polynomial}
\end{equation}
and define the word
\begin{equation}
w_n=n\,1\,2\cdots(n-2)\,n\,1\,0\,
(n-1)(n-2)\cdots2\,0\,n.
\label{eq:cubic-unbounded-parry-word}
\end{equation}
Thus $|w_n|=2n+2$.

submission_metadata.md-24-
submission_metadata.md-25-Abstract:
submission_metadata.md:26:We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. This is not numerical beta-value normalization in Z[beta]. For every quadratic Pisot base, we prove that the overlap threshold is three exactly for the roots of x^2-ax-a and x^2-ax+1, and is two otherwise. For arbitrary nonintegral simple-Parry Pisot bases, an exact finite collision graph determines the optimal causal inverse length. This length is unbounded already in degree three: if beta_n in (n,n+1) is the root of x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n and m_n=n-1, then the aperture-m_n recoding is injective and has optimal causal inverse length n-1. The proof uses a parameter-uniform two-window carry exclusion and an exact terminal collision-path classification.

# Stage A Scope Contract

Paper directory: `D:\omega\automath\papers\publication\2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds`

Target journal: DCDS-A.

This contract fixes the Stage A scope for the DCDS-A article. It is a contract for what the article must prove, what it may cite or use only as support, and what must be deferred to sister-paper pipelines. It is not a referee report and it does not authorize weakening, deleting, demoting, renaming, or moving theorem environments.

## Central Research Question

For the canonical finite-window Fibonacci stabilization map `Fold_m : {0,1}^m -> X_m`, where `X_m` is the golden-mean legal language and `Fold_m` selects the unique length-`m` admissible representative with the same Fibonacci valuation modulo `F_{m+2}`, determine exactly when the sliding stabilized-window factor
`Phi_m : ({0,1}^Z, sigma) -> (Y_m, sigma)` becomes a finite-memory topological conjugacy onto a subshift of finite type, classify the unique failure below threshold, identify the intrinsic right-resolving presentation of the image, and explain why the golden two-window obstruction is exceptional inside the metallic family.

The article owns the sharp `m=3` threshold, the arithmetic decoder at `m=3`, the `m>=3` finite-memory two-sided conjugacy, the full `m=2` branch-locus classification, the right Fischer cover identification of `Y_m`, and the metallic two-window rigidity theorem. Quantitative residue, Fourier, second-moment, entropy, Sturmian discrepancy, and transport statements are in scope only insofar as they support or structurally exploit this conjugacy theorem.

## Target-Journal Publication Bar

For DCDS-A, the paper must read as a structural symbolic-dynamics article with arithmetic content, not as a physics-motivation paper and not as a broad enumeration or anomaly survey. The minimum publication bar is:

- A self-contained theorem chain proving the exact phase transition:
  `m=2` has one branch orbit pair and all other path-space fibers are singleton; every `m>=3` has a finite-memory conjugacy onto an SFT; no intermediate degeneration exists.
- An explicit arithmetic proof of `thm:block-invertibility` with `lem:m3-decoder` as the visible core, rather than a generic resolving-theory corollary.
- A complete proof of `thm:two-sided-conjugacy`, including local decoder `cor:explicit-decoder`, SFT memory bound, invariant measure transport, fixed-point/zeta consequences, and entropy preservation.
- A complete proof that the natural overlap presentation is the right Fischer cover of `Y_m` with `2^{m-1}` forced states, follower separation, intrinsic synchronization, and minimality among right-resolving presentations.
- A complete metallic-family comparison proving that `A=1` is the unique constant-type metallic value for which two-window normalization fails to be a sliding-block conjugacy.
- Clean scope positioning against sister papers so that duplicate-looking fiber arithmetic, gauge anomaly, Berstel-adder normalization, Sturmian discrepancy, and rotation TV material is intentionally cited or placed as support, not silently re-owned.
- Correct DCDS-A-facing metadata and framing: cover letter target, title alignment, MSC classification, bibliography naming, and introduction order must no longer carry Nonlinearity/JPA inheritance.

## Structural Bad Examples and Their Role

The paper should use bad examples as structure drivers, not as loose warnings.

- `m=2`: `0^Z` and `1^Z` both map to the all-`00` output. This is the complete branch locus and the support of the entropy/KL defect.
- `m=3,n=2`: `0001` and `0110` both map to `(000,001)`. This proves the finite-block threshold `n>=m` is sharp even at the first invertible aperture.
- `m=3` decoder: the exceptional residue branch `q=2` must remain explicit and separated by `(r_0,r_2)`.
- `m>=4` decoder: the possible values of `q_t` split into the finite-budget disjoint alternatives `{0,1,2}` and `{F_m,F_m+1,F_m+2}`, forcing the boundary bit.
- Metallic `A>=2`: local solvability is forced by the disjoint alternatives `{0}` and `{A-1,A}`; the golden case collapses this distinction and produces the branch.
- Gauge anomaly `110 -> 001`: if mentioned, it must be described only as an obstruction to naive cross-resolution truncation, not as a DCDS-A invariant.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact finite verification for the simple-Parry causal obstructions.

All collision calculations use integer arithmetic.  A tuple ``digits`` is the
finite greedy expansion d_beta(1)=t_1...t_p 0^infinity.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from itertools import product


def cubic_family_digits(n: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Return the finite Parry word for the cubic family indexed by ``n``."""
    if n < 4:
        raise ValueError("the cubic family begins at n=4")
    return tuple(
        [n]
        + list(range(1, n - 1))
        + [n, 1, 0]
        + list(range(n - 1, 1, -1))
        + [0, n]
    )


def cubic_family_q_sequence(n: int, maximum: int) -> list[int]:
    """Return the cubic-family language counts through ``maximum``."""
    return q_sequence(cubic_family_digits(n), maximum)


def cubic_family_extremal_vector(n: int, aperture: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Return the extremal length-(aperture-1) collision path."""
    if n < 4 or not 2 <= aperture <= n - 1:
        raise ValueError("require n>=4 and 2<=aperture<=n-1")
    if aperture == 2:
        return (2, n)
    padding = aperture - 3
    return tuple(
        [-2] * padding + [n - 2, -2, -n, 1] + [0] * padding
    )


def _polynomial_product(left: list[int], right: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Multiply low-to-high integer coefficient lists."""
    result = [0] * (len(left) + len(right) - 1)
    for i, left_coefficient in enumerate(left):
        for j, right_coefficient in enumerate(right):
            result[i + j] += left_coefficient * right_coefficient
    return result


def cubic_family_claims(n: int) -> dict[str, bool | int]:
    """Check the Parry factorization and suffix inequalities for one index."""
    digits = cubic_family_digits(n)
    parry = [-digit for digit in reversed(digits)] + [1]
    minimal = [-n, 2 * n, -(n + 2), 1]
    geometric_n = [1] * n
    geometric_n1 = [1] * (n + 1)
    factored = _polynomial_product(
        _polynomial_product(minimal, geometric_n), geometric_n1
    )

    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
    suffixes_are_smaller = all(
        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
        for start in range(1, len(digits))
    )
    return {
        "parry_factorization": parry == factored,
        "proper_suffixes_are_smaller": suffixes_are_smaller,
        "parry_length": len(digits),
    }


def q_sequence(digits: tuple[int, ...], n: int) -> list[int]:
    """Return Q_0,...,Q_n for a finite Parry word."""
    p = len(digits)
    if p < 1 or digits[-1] <= 0:
        raise ValueError("the finite Parry word must have positive last digit")
    q = [1]
    for k in range(1, n + 1):
        recurrence = sum(digits[i - 1] * q[k - i] for i in range(1, min(k, p) + 1))
        q.append(recurrence + (1 if k < p else 0))
    return q


def bounded_multiple_order(digits: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    """Verify and return the bounded-multiple order of the companion polynomial."""
    d = digits[0]
    if d < 1 or any(not 0 <= digit <= d for digit in digits):
        raise ValueError("digits must lie in the greedy alphabet")
    coefficients = (-digits[-1],) + tuple(-digit for digit in reversed(digits[:-1])) + (1,)
    if coefficients[0] == 0 or max(map(abs, coefficients)) > d:
        raise AssertionError("the companion polynomial does not meet the coefficient bound")
    # Every nonzero element of (P) has degree at least deg(P) in Z[z].
    return len(digits)


def _is_legal_low_to_high(digits: tuple[int, ...], word: tuple[int, ...]) -> bool:
    """Apply Parry's suffix test to a finite word in low-to-high order."""
    period = digits[:-1] + (digits[-1] - 1,)
    high_to_low = word[::-1]
    for start in range(len(high_to_low)):
        suffix = high_to_low[start:]
        boundary = tuple(period[j % len(period)] for j in range(len(suffix)))
        if suffix > boundary:
            return False
    return True


def rank_is_consecutive(digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int) -> bool:
    """Check the colex rank formula against the complete legal language."""
    d = digits[0]
    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
    ranks = [
        sum(word[j] * q[j] for j in range(m))
        for word in product(range(d + 1), repeat=m)
        if _is_legal_low_to_high(digits, word)
    ]
    return sorted(ranks) == list(range(q[m]))

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }
+

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

 Abstract:
-We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. This is not numerical beta-value normalization in Z[beta]. For every quadratic Pisot base, we prove that the overlap threshold is three exactly for the roots of x^2-ax-a and x^2-ax+1, and is two otherwise. For arbitrary nonintegral simple-Parry Pisot bases, an exact finite collision graph determines the optimal causal inverse length. +We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. +def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }
+

+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:

+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four

+hypothesis removal.

+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]

+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.

+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[

+\]

+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and

+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and

# Stage A Theorem Inventory

Paper: `2026_sharp_three_window_threshold_fibonacci_conjugacy_dcds`

Target journal: DCDS-A.

## Summary

The manuscript now has one arithmetic spine.  It proves the exact overlap
threshold for every quadratic Pisot cyclic rank recoding and then shows that
optimal causal inverse length is unbounded already in algebraic degree three.
For `M_n(x)=x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n`, its root `beta_n in (n,n+1)`, and
`m_n=n-1`, Theorem `thm:cubic-unbounded-causal-depth` proves that `beta_n` is
a nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot number, `Phi_{beta_n,m_n}` is
injective, and `ell_cau(beta_n,m_n)=n-1` for every `n>=4`.

The prior DCDS-A theorem chain is retained as the golden special case and as
support: the finite-window definitions, residue/Fourier fiber arithmetic,
sliding factor and overlap graph, explicit `m=3` decoder, sharp Fibonacci
block invertibility for `m>=3`, complete `m=2` branch-locus classification,
two-sided finite-memory conjugacy onto an SFT, phase-transition package,
standard dynamical consequences, metallic two-window rigidity, and the
Fischer-cover theorem.

No proof gap remains in the quadratic threshold or cubic unbounded-depth
chains.  The remaining interfaces are explicit rather than silently asserted:

- Publication-facing Lean wrappers for the three new family labels have not
  been created; their status is paper-level pending.
- A parameter-uniform two-output decoder in the negative-conjugate quadratic
  chamber at apertures `m>=4` remains open; the proved bound there is
  `2<=ell_cau<=m`.
- Several support-only appendix interfaces predate this deepening and remain
  outside the new headline theorem chain.

## Core Present Results

- `thm:cubic-unbounded-causal-depth`: the explicit degree-three family above
  has injective aperture `m_n=n-1` and exact causal length `n-1`; hence no
  uniform causal-depth bound exists among injective cubic simple-Parry folds.
- `lem:cubic-unbounded-two-window`: parameter-uniform exclusion of a nonzero
  second carry for every `n>=4` and `2<=r<=n-1`.
- `lem:cubic-unbounded-terminal-paths`: exact terminal classification
  `K_{n,r,r-1}={0,+/-E_{n,r}}` and `K_{n,r,r}={0}`.
- `thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold`: the threshold is three exactly for
  `x^2-ax-a` and `x^2-ax+1`, and two for every other quadratic Pisot base.

- `def:metallic-conjugacy-threshold`: the least nontrivial aperture `m>=2`;
  aperture one is explicitly excluded because every one-symbol fold is the
  identity.
- `thm:metallic-family-block-bijection`: for integer `A>=1`, `m>=2`,
  `(A,m)!=(1,2)`, and every `n>=m`, the finite-block map is injective and
  `|L_n(Y_{A,m})|=(A+1)^(n+m-1)`.  The proof treats `m=2`, `m=3`, and `m>=4`
  separately and retains `lem:m3-decoder` at the golden endpoint.
- `thm:metallic-threshold-classification`: under the exact data of
  `def:metallic-window-data`, the conjugacy apertures are all `m>=3` for
  `A=1` and all `m>=2` for `A>=2`; hence the golden mean is uniquely
  characterized by `m_*=3`.  The inverse has memory zero and anticipation
  `m-1`, and every image is an SFT with forbidden length at most `m+1`.
- `thm:metallic-entropy-zeta-extremality`: all family images have entropy
  `log(A+1)`; the unique exceptional pair has fixed-point counts `2^n-1` and
  zeta `(1-z)/(1-2z)`, while every conjugate case has fixed-point counts
  `(A+1)^n` and zeta `1/(1-(A+1)z)`.
- `rem:metallic-beta-scope`: the proved beta-family is explicitly limited to
  the norm-`-1` metallic units.  Arbitrary quadratic Pisot numbers with other
  digit or Parry data are an open formulation interface, not an asserted
  extension.

- `def:Xm`, `def:valuation`, `prop:finite-window-range`: finite golden-mean language, valuation, and finite-window Zeckendorf range.
- `def:fold`, `def:fiber-notation-and-residue-counts`: canonical stabilization and fiber/residue notation.
- `thm:fiber-residue`, `thm:fiber-dft`: residue fibers and roots-of-unity Fourier formula.
- `thm:affine-transfer`, `cor:affine-transfer-stats`: shifted-weight affine transfer.
- `def:Phi`, `def:overlap-graph`, `thm:finite-state-lift`: sliding factor and bi-resolving overlap presentation.
- `lem:m3-decoder`: explicit three-window arithmetic decoder.
- `thm:block-invertibility`, `cor:explicit-decoder`: sharp threshold and memory-0 anticipation-`m-1` inverse.
- `prop:low-window-counterexamples`: the `m=2` sequence collapse and `m=3,n=2` finite-block collision.
- `thm:m2-branch-locus`, `cor:m2-defect-formulas`, `cor:m2-asymptotic-sufficiency`, `cor:m2-mod-zero`: full two-window branch analysis and defects.
- `thm:two-sided-conjugacy`, `thm:phase-transition`, `prop:conjugacy-consequences`, `prop:measure-entropy-preservation`, `cor:entropy-preservation`: SFT conjugacy, no intermediate degeneration, zeta/periodic/invariant-measure consequences, and entropy.
- `thm:metallic-two-window-rigidity`: the prior `A>=2`, `m=2` rigidity result,
  now a supporting small-aperture case of the family classification.
- `thm:fischer-cover-stabilized-image`: intrinsic synchronizing words, follower separation, right Fischer cover, and `2^(m-1)` state lower bound.
- `thm:exact-sufficiency`, `cor:path-space-divergence`, `thm:continuous-potentials`, `prop:finite-range-renorm`: currently included measurement/transport consequences.
- `prop:second-moment-recurrence`, `prop:uniform-collision`: finite-fiber second-moment and collision support.

## Weak Or Incomplete Interfaces

- `thm:fold-suite`: present with `\leanverified{paper_fibonacci_stabilization_fold_suite}`, but the body only cites another manuscript. Since the scope contract requires Fold_m well-definedness, idempotence, surjectivity, and fiber partition inside this paper, this needs a self-contained proof or a fully stated proof body.
- `thm:m2-branch-locus`: the classification is present, but the initial Fold_2 rule is imported by citation. The rule is short and should be computed directly.
- `def:fiber-lift` and `thm:kl-ledger`: currently citation interfaces. This is acceptable only if the entropy ledger is explicitly support-only.
- `thm:tv-certificate`, `prop:boundary-layer`, `thm:operational-observable-recovery`, `cor:tv-bounded-type`: support-only discrepancy/TV labels are mostly citation stubs. They should not be presented as owned core results unless full proofs are supplied.
- `prop:finite-range-renorm`: the proof establishes range at most `r+m-1`; exact minimal range is not proved.

## Split Or Excluded Material

- `sections_jpa/A4_gauge_anomaly.tex`: gauge anomaly, worst-case anomaly, and empirical `S_m` recurrence belong to a gauge/spectral-fingerprint pipeline unless fold-aware descent is proved.
- `sections_jpa/06_addressing.tex`: synchronization, occupancy, and collision-limited addressing belong to an addressing/auditable-addressing paper.
- `sections_jpa/A6_tv_extensions.tex`: coarse free-energy and golden optimality among metallic means are rotation-TV/extremal support, not part of the present DCDS-A theorem chain unless a human later chooses that scope.
- `sections_jpa/07c_generalization.tex`: general Ostrowski finite-window templates should remain an outlook, not an in-scope theorem.
- `sections_jpa/A3_uniform_benchmarks.tex` and `sections_jpa/A5_uniform_collision.tex`: benchmark/collision material duplicates or forces split-paper anomaly/addressing content.

\begin{letter}{Editorial Board\\Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series A (DCDS-A)}

\opening{Dear Editors,}

We submit our manuscript entitled

\medskip
\centerline{\textbf{Overlap thresholds and unbounded causal depth}}
\centerline{\textbf{for cyclic ranks of Pisot $\beta$-languages}}
\medskip

\noindent for consideration in \textit{Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series A} (DCDS-A).

The paper defines a cyclic ordered-language-rank recoding for Pisot
$\beta$-languages and proves sharp overlap and causal-depth results.  The
recoding is expressly distinguished from numerical $\beta$-normalization in
$\mathbb Z[\beta]$.  The main contributions are:

\begin{itemize}
\item A complete two-chamber classification for all quadratic Pisot bases:
the threshold is three exactly for $x^2-ax-a$ and $x^2-ax+1$, and is two
otherwise.  Above threshold the finite-block maps are injective and the
sliding recoding has a memory-zero future inverse.

\item An explicit family of nonintegral cubic simple-Parry Pisot bases with
unbounded exact causal inverse length.  If $\beta_n\in(n,n+1)$ is the root of
$x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n$ and $m_n=n-1$, then the aperture-$m_n$ map is injective
and its optimal causal inverse length is exactly $n-1$.

\item A complete classification of the unique exceptional pair $(A,m)=(1,2)$: injectivity fails on exactly one branch orbit, with exact conditional entropy and Kullback--Leibler defect formulas. Its zeta function is $(1-z)/(1-2z)$, whereas every conjugate case has the corresponding full-shift zeta function.

\item A coupled interval-rank induction for the positive-conjugate language, a
nearest-multiple separation lemma for both recurrence signs, and an explicit
two-output decoder at every nonextremal two-window parameter.

\item Four complete nonmetallic examples and a Fischer-cover identification
for the presented Fibonacci output shift.  Routine entropy, pressure,
Blackwell-equivalence, and discrepancy consequences are separated into
supplementary material.
\end{itemize}

We believe the manuscript fits the scope of \textit{Discrete and Continuous Dynamical Systems - Series A} (DCDS-A) because it is a structural symbolic-dynamics paper with explicit finite-rank arithmetic.  The ordered-language construction is compared directly with abstract numeration and Bertrand systems, while the quadratic threshold and unbounded cubic collision-depth theorems are map-specific results.

The manuscript is original, has not been published previously, and is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests.

\closing{Sincerely,}

\end{letter}
\end{document}

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5

+    }

+\begin{proof}

+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number

+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed

+hypothesis removal.

+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]

+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and

+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.

+We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. This is not numerical beta-value normalization in Z[beta]. For every quadratic Pisot base, we prove that the overlap threshold is three exactly for the roots of x^2-ax-a and x^2-ax+1, and is two otherwise. For arbitrary nonintegral simple-Parry bases, without a Pisot hypothesis, an exact finite collision graph determines the optimal causal inverse length. This length is unbounded already in degree three: if beta_n in (n,n+1) is the root of x^3-(n+2)x^2+2nx-n and m_n=n-1, then the aperture-m_n recoding is injective and has optimal causal inverse length n-1. The proof uses a parameter-uniform two-window carry exclusion and an exact terminal collision-path classification.
 
 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification:
 Primary: 37B10, 37B40; Secondary: 11B39, 37A35, 11A67, 11K38

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }
+

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

The universal minorant of M$(α)$ obtained is $θ_η^{-1} > 1$, for some integer $η\geq 259$, where $θ_η$ is the positive real root of $-1+x+x^η$. The set of Salem numbers is shown to be bounded from below by the Perron number $θ_{31}^{-1} = 1.08545\ldots$, dominant root of the trinomial $-1 - z^{30} + z^{31}$. Whether Lehmer's number is the smallest Salem number remains open. For sequences of algebraic integers of Mahler measure smaller than the smallest Pisot number $Θ= 1.3247\ldots$, whose houses have a dynamical degree tending to infinity, the Galois orbit measures of conjugates are proved to converge towards the Haar measure on $|z|=1$ (limit equidistribution).The dynamical zeta function is used to investigate the domain of very small Mahler measures of algebraic integers in the range (1, 1.176280 . . .], if any.

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}

+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

2024 | Miyanohara, Eiji | A note on non-periodic greedy expansions in Salem base
The greedy \(\beta\)-expansion \(x = \sum_{i=1}^\infty a_i \beta^{-i}\) is eventually periodic for each \(x \in \mathbb{Q}(\beta) \cap [0,1)\) when the real base \(\beta > 1\) is a Pisot number, and it is an open question whether this also holds for Salem bases. The author shows that if the sequence \(a_1a_2\cdots\) is aperiodic, then its factor complexity \(p(n)\) satisfies \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} \log p(n) \ge \frac{1}{\deg(\beta)} \log \beta\), by constructing elements of \(\mathbb{Q}(\beta)\) that would approximate \(x\) too well otherwise.

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

-We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. +## Tier-2 audit: externally posed open problems and actual interfaces
+
+Checked: 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+### Search record and open status
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for Salem-number beta expansions, purely
+periodic Pisot expansions, weak finiteness, Property (F), and the Pisot
+substitution conjecture.  Primary sources arXiv:1411.2419, arXiv:1912.10386,
+arXiv:1810.03500, arXiv:2206.06675, and arXiv:2603.19554 were inspected in
+full text.  Crossref and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 and are recorded as
+rate-limited, not as zero-result searches.  Semantic Scholar returned the
+records for DOI `10.4064/aa8260-11-2017`, `10.1112/blms/12.4.269`, and
+`10.1017/etds.2016.44`; its citation graph lists only two citations of
+Hejda--Steiner, neither claiming a solution of the questions below.  The
+zbMATH Open API was searched for `purely periodic Pisot`, `Pisot substitution
+conjecture`, and `Salem Parry Schmidt`.  Its post-2018 real-base results do
+not report a resolution of the Hejda--Steiner questions.  Its review of E.
+Miyanohara, *A note on non-periodic greedy expansions in Salem base*, Res.
+Number Theory **10** (2024), DOI `10.1007/s40993-024-00507-8`, still calls
+Salem eventual periodicity an open question.  The 2022 result arXiv:2206.06675
+proves that a positive-density set of powers of a Salem number are Parry,
+not that the Salem number itself is Parry.  These checks support the open
+status assertions below as of the audit date.
+
+### Four printed questions
+
+1. **Schmidt's Salem--Parry conjecture.**  K. Schmidt, *On periodic
+   expansions of Pisot numbers and Salem numbers*, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc.
+   **12** (1980), 269--278, DOI `10.1112/blms/12.4.269`.  Stockton's explicit
+   statement of Schmidt's conjecture in *On the co-factors of degree 6 Salem
+   number beta expansions*, J. Integer Seq. **24** (2021), Article 21.2.2,
+   arXiv:1912.10386, reads: "Schmidt conjectured that the same was true for
+   Salem numbers," where "the same" is that `beta` is a Parry number, i.e.
+   `d_beta(1)` is eventually periodic.  Stockton adds: "it is still not known
+   for any degree greater than 4."
+
+2. **Hejda--Steiner Question (A).**  T. Hejda and W. Steiner,
+   *Beta-expansions of rational numbers in quadratic Pisot bases*, Acta Arith.
+   **183** (2018), 35--51, DOI `10.4064/aa8260-11-2017`, arXiv:1411.2419,
+   p. 50: "Prove or disprove that $\gamma(\beta)=1$ for quadratic Pisot number
+   $\beta>1$, a root of $\beta^2=a\beta+b$, if and only if
+   $a/b\in\mathbb Z$ and $a\ge b^2$ or
+   $(a,b)\in\{(24,6),(30,6)\}$."
+
+3. **Hejda--Steiner Question (B).**  Same citation and page: "For which
+   quadratic $\beta$ we have that $\gamma(\beta)=0$? Can we drop the
+   restrictions on $a$ and $b$ in Theorem 2? More specifically, is it true
+   that $a<\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}b$ implies $\gamma(\beta)=0$?"
+
+4. **Hejda--Steiner Question (C).**  Same citation and page: "What is the
+   structure of the prefixes of $\beta$-adic expansions of integers for a
+   general quadratic $\beta$?"
+
+### Machinery-to-problem map
+
+- **Schmidt.**  The finite Parry word and recurrence used in
+  `thm:simple-parry-causal-collision` exist only after the desired eventual
+  periodicity (and, in the paper, the stronger simple-Parry property) is
+  known.  The collision graph can analyze a Salem base already known to be
+  simple Parry, but it supplies no bounded orbit for `T_beta(1)`.  The missing
+  step is exactly the conjecture, so applying the graph would be circular.
+- **Question (A).**  `prop:parry-rank-bijection` and
+  `thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold` cover precisely the roots
+  `beta^2=a beta+b` and give their legal languages and count recurrence.
+  However, `gamma(beta)` is defined by equality of real beta-values and the
+  beta-natural-extension domain.  The paper reduces an integer language rank
+  modulo `Q_m`.  A bridge would have to identify these congruence fibers with
+  beta-adic/natural-extension fibers or establish the required tile-boundary
+  inclusion; no such identity is present, and the paper gives an explicit
+  example showing rank congruence does not preserve beta-value.
+- **Question (B).**  The nearest-multiple separation lemma controls multiples
+  of the integer word count `Q_m`, not the conjugate-coordinate extrema that
+  determine `gamma(beta)`.  What is missing is a uniform beta-tile boundary
+  estimate in the parameter range `a<phi b`.  None of the sliding congruence
+  estimates has that geometric conclusion.
+- **Question (C).**  The closest objects are the standard Parry language,
+  its colex rank, and the prefix counts `Q_m`.  The paper's cyclic rank fold
+  discards the compatible inverse-system data needed for a beta-adic integer.
+  A canonical map would require compatibility of the residues as `m` varies;
+  the current moduli `Q_m` do not divide one another, and no bonding maps are
+  proved.  Thus the finite-window results do not determine beta-adic prefix
+  structure.
+
+### A/B/C/D assessment and selected route
+
+- **(A):** no named problem above is honestly touched beyond sharing the
+  Parry language.  The numerical-value, natural-extension, or substitution
+  geometry needed by each is absent.
+- **(B):** the input full shift, greedy beta-language, Parry word, language
+  counts, and colex ordered-language rank are standard.  The reduction modulo
+  `Q_m` is bespoke.  Above threshold the image is canonically conjugate back
+  to a full shift, so it does not yield a new invariant of a standard
+  beta-system.  There is no canonical map to numerical beta-normalization.
+- **(C):** the Pisot hypothesis in the exact collision criterion, causal
+  completeness, bounded-multiple order, and aperture-two trichotomy is an
+  artifact: their proofs use only simple-Parry language/rank data and finite
+  congruence graphs.  The simple-Parry hypothesis itself is real because it
+  supplies the finite recurrence and positional colex rank used by the graph.
+- **(D):** the negative-conjugate conjecture `ell_cau(beta,m)=2` for `m>=4`
+  remains plausible, but a proof would sharpen only the bespoke decoder and
+  the current carry analysis does not exhaust the nonzero constant-carry
+  branches.  No plausible converse links overlap injectivity to a standard
+  beta-expansion property.
+
+Route **(C)** was selected as the best product of feasibility and impact.
+Proposition `prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope` removes Pisot from the four
+general simple-Parry results.  Strictness is proved using the irreducible
+non-Pisot simple-Parry polynomial `x^4-2x^3-2`, for which
+`d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity` and `ell_cau(beta,2)=2`.  This is a genuine
+hypothesis removal, but it does not solve a named problem and does not by
+itself move the paper to Tier 2.

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }
+

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

 Abstract:
-We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. This is not numerical beta-value normalization in Z[beta]. +We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows. +## Tier-2 audit: externally posed open problems and actual interfaces
+
+Checked: 2026-08-14 (Asia/Singapore).
+
+### Search record and open status
+
+The arXiv Atom API was queried for Salem-number beta expansions, purely
+periodic Pisot expansions, weak finiteness, Property (F), and the Pisot
+substitution conjecture.  Primary sources arXiv:1411.2419, arXiv:1912.10386,
+arXiv:1810.03500, arXiv:2206.06675, and arXiv:2603.19554 were inspected in
+full text.  Crossref and OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 and are recorded as
+rate-limited, not as zero-result searches.  Semantic Scholar returned the
+records for DOI `10.4064/aa8260-11-2017`, `10.1112/blms/12.4.269`, and
+`10.1017/etds.2016.44`; its citation graph lists only two citations of
+Hejda--Steiner, neither claiming a solution of the questions below.  The
+zbMATH Open API was searched for `purely periodic Pisot`, `Pisot substitution
+conjecture`, and `Salem Parry Schmidt`.  Its post-2018 real-base results do
+not report a resolution of the Hejda--Steiner questions.  Its review of E.
+Miyanohara, *A note on non-periodic greedy expansions in Salem base*, Res.
+Number Theory **10** (2024), DOI `10.1007/s40993-024-00507-8`, still calls
+Salem eventual periodicity an open question.  The 2022 result arXiv:2206.06675
+proves that a positive-density set of powers of a Salem number are Parry,
+not that the Salem number itself is Parry.  These checks support the open
+status assertions below as of the audit date.
+
+### Four printed questions
+
+1. **Schmidt's Salem--Parry conjecture.**  K. Schmidt, *On periodic
+   expansions of Pisot numbers and Salem numbers*, Bull. Lond. Math. Soc.
+   **12** (1980), 269--278, DOI `10.1112/blms/12.4.269`.  Stockton's explicit
+   statement of Schmidt's conjecture in *On the co-factors of degree 6 Salem
+   number beta expansions*, J. Integer Seq. **24** (2021), Article 21.2.2,
+   arXiv:1912.10386, reads: "Schmidt conjectured that the same was true for
+   Salem numbers," where "the same" is that `beta` is a Parry number, i.e.
+   `d_beta(1)` is eventually periodic.  Stockton adds: "it is still not known
+   for any degree greater than 4."
+
+2. **Hejda--Steiner Question (A).**  T. Hejda and W. Steiner,
+   *Beta-expansions of rational numbers in quadratic Pisot bases*, Acta Arith.
+   **183** (2018), 35--51, DOI `10.4064/aa8260-11-2017`, arXiv:1411.2419,
+   p. 50: "Prove or disprove that $\gamma(\beta)=1$ for quadratic Pisot number
+   $\beta>1$, a root of $\beta^2=a\beta+b$, if and only if
+   $a/b\in\mathbb Z$ and $a\ge b^2$ or
+   $(a,b)\in\{(24,6),(30,6)\}$."
+
+3. **Hejda--Steiner Question (B).**  Same citation and page: "For which
+   quadratic $\beta$ we have that $\gamma(\beta)=0$? Can we drop the
+   restrictions on $a$ and $b$ in Theorem 2? More specifically, is it true
+   that $a<\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}b$ implies $\gamma(\beta)=0$?"
+
+4. **Hejda--Steiner Question (C).**  Same citation and page: "What is the
+   structure of the prefixes of $\beta$-adic expansions of integers for a
+   general quadratic $\beta$?"
+
+### Machinery-to-problem map
+
+- **Schmidt.**  The finite Parry word and recurrence used in
+  `thm:simple-parry-causal-collision` exist only after the desired eventual
+  periodicity (and, in the paper, the stronger simple-Parry property) is
+  known.  The collision graph can analyze a Salem base already known to be
+  simple Parry, but it supplies no bounded orbit for `T_beta(1)`.  The missing
+  step is exactly the conjecture, so applying the graph would be circular.
+- **Question (A).**  `prop:parry-rank-bijection` and
+  `thm:full-quadratic-pisot-threshold` cover precisely the roots
+  `beta^2=a beta+b` and give their legal languages and count recurrence.
+  However, `gamma(beta)` is defined by equality of real beta-values and the
+  beta-natural-extension domain.  The paper reduces an integer language rank
+  modulo `Q_m`.  A bridge would have to identify these congruence fibers with
+  beta-adic/natural-extension fibers or establish the required tile-boundary
+  inclusion; no such identity is present, and the paper gives an explicit
+  example showing rank congruence does not preserve beta-value.
+- **Question (B).**  The nearest-multiple separation lemma controls multiples
+  of the integer word count `Q_m`, not the conjugate-coordinate extrema that
+  determine `gamma(beta)`.  What is missing is a uniform beta-tile boundary
+  estimate in the parameter range `a<phi b`.  None of the sliding congruence
+  estimates has that geometric conclusion.
+- **Question (C).**  The closest objects are the standard Parry language,
+  its colex rank, and the prefix counts `Q_m`.  The paper's cyclic rank fold
+  discards the compatible inverse-system data needed for a beta-adic integer.
+  A canonical map would require compatibility of the residues as `m` varies;
+  the current moduli `Q_m` do not divide one another, and no bonding maps are
+  proved.  Thus the finite-window results do not determine beta-adic prefix
+  structure.
+
+### A/B/C/D assessment and selected route
+
+- **(A):** no named problem above is honestly touched beyond sharing the
+  Parry language.  The numerical-value, natural-extension, or substitution
+  geometry needed by each is absent.
+- **(B):** the input full shift, greedy beta-language, Parry word, language
+  counts, and colex ordered-language rank are standard.  The reduction modulo
+  `Q_m` is bespoke.  Above threshold the image is canonically conjugate back
+  to a full shift, so it does not yield a new invariant of a standard
+  beta-system.  There is no canonical map to numerical beta-normalization.
+- **(C):** the Pisot hypothesis in the exact collision criterion, causal
+  completeness, bounded-multiple order, and aperture-two trichotomy is an
+  artifact: their proofs use only simple-Parry language/rank data and finite
+  congruence graphs.  The simple-Parry hypothesis itself is real because it
+  supplies the finite recurrence and positional colex rank used by the graph.
+- **(D):** the negative-conjugate conjecture `ell_cau(beta,m)=2` for `m>=4`
+  remains plausible, but a proof would sharpen only the bespoke decoder and
+  the current carry analysis does not exhaust the nonzero constant-carry
+  branches.  No plausible converse links overlap injectivity to a standard

+def non_pisot_simple_parry_claims() -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Verify the strict non-Pisot witness d_beta(1)=2002 0^infinity."""
+    digits = (2, 0, 0, 2)
+    boundary = digits + (0,) * len(digits)
+    parry_admissible = all(
+        digits[start:] + (0,) * (len(digits) + start) < boundary
+        for start in range(1, len(digits))
+    )
+
+    def bisect_root(function, left: float, right: float) -> float:
+        for _ in range(80):
+            midpoint = (left + right) / 2
+            if function(midpoint) > 0:
+                right = midpoint
+            else:
+                left = midpoint
+        return (left + right) / 2
+
+    beta = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 - 2 * x**3 - 2, 2.0, 2.2)
+    negative_root_modulus = bisect_root(lambda x: x**4 + 2 * x**3 - 2, 0.0, 1.0)
+    complex_root_modulus = (2 / (beta * negative_root_modulus)) ** 0.5
+    aperture_two = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    return {
+        "digits": digits,
+        "parry_admissible": parry_admissible,
+        "is_pisot": complex_root_modulus < 1,
+        "largest_nondominant_modulus": max(
+            negative_root_modulus, complex_root_modulus
+        ),
+        "q_prefix": q_sequence(digits, 6),
+        "rank_checks": [rank_is_consecutive(digits, m) for m in range(1, 7)],
+        "aperture_two_causal_length": aperture_two["causal_length"],
+    }
+

+\begin{proposition}[Pisot-free scope is strict]
+\label{prop:nonpisot-simple-parry-scope}
+Proposition~\ref{prop:simple-parry-bounded-order},
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision}, Corollary
+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}, and Theorem
+\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} hold for every nonintegral simple-Parry
+number; no Pisot hypothesis is required.  This strictly enlarges their scope.
+Indeed, let $\beta$ be the positive root of
+\begin{equation}
+x^4-2x^3-2=0.
+\label{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness}
+\end{equation}
+Then
+\[
+d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty,
+\]
+$\beta$ is not Pisot, and the aperture-two cyclic rank fold is injective with
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proposition}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence for $Q_n$, the consecutive colex-rank formula, and Parry
+admissibility used above hold for every simple-Parry number
+\cite{Parry1960,CharlierCisterninoStipulanti2022}.  The proofs of the four
+listed results subsequently use only these data, the full raw alphabet
+$\{0,\ldots,d\}$, integer congruences modulo $Q_m$, and finite directed
+graphs.  No estimate on a Galois conjugate occurs.  This proves the claimed
+hypothesis removal.
+
+It remains to show that the enlargement is strict.  The polynomial in
+\eqref{eq:nonpisot-simple-parry-witness} is Eisenstein at $2$, hence
+irreducible.  Its positive root satisfies
+\[
+2<\beta<\frac{11}{5},
+\]
+because the polynomial takes the values $-2$ and $81/625$ at the two
+endpoints.  Its defining equation gives
+\[
+1=2\beta^{-1}+2\beta^{-4}.
+\]
+The proper suffixes of $2002\,0^\infty$ are all lexicographically smaller
+than $2002\,0^\infty$: the first two begin with $0$, while the third is
+$2000^\infty<2002\,0^\infty$.  Parry's criterion therefore gives
+$d_\beta(1)=2002\,0^\infty$.
+
+Write the negative real root as $-u$.  The function
+$g(u)=u^4+2u^3-2$ is strictly increasing for $u>0$, with $g(0)<0<g(1)$,
+so $0<u<1$.  The two remaining roots are a nonreal conjugate pair
+$z,\overline z$.  Moreover,
+\[
+\beta^4 g(2/\beta)
+=4(3+4\beta-\beta^3)>0,
+\]
+where the last inequality follows from
+$\beta<11/5$ and
+$3+4\beta-\beta^3>11-(11/5)^3=44/125$.
+Thus $u<2/\beta$.  The product of the four roots is $-2$, whence
+\[
+|z|^2=\frac{2}{\beta u}>1.
+\]
+Irreducibility makes $z$ a Galois conjugate of $\beta$, so $\beta$ is not
+Pisot.  Finally $d=2$, $p=4$, and
+$c_\beta=t_2+1=1<d$; case~\textup{(b)} of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} yields injectivity and
+$\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+\end{proof}

 Abstract:
-We study a cyclic rank recoding of greedy beta-languages: ordered-language ranks are extended to the full digit cube, reduced modulo the number of legal words, and overlapped along consecutive windows.
